RECORDS

WEDNESDAY, MAY 11, 1904
The first executive session of Psi Upsilon Convention was called to order
at 2:30 P.M., in the Rho Chapter House, by Bro. Herbert L. Bridgman, of
the Executive Council. Bro. John T. Johnston, of the Rho, was appointed
Temporary President, and Bro. John W. Mapel, of the Rho, Temporary
Recorder.

The Temporary President appointed the following Committees ;
On Credentials Bro. Bass (M), Chairman ; Bro. Barnard {H), Bro. Bufflngton {BB).
On Permanent Organization Bro. Baker (r). Chairman ; Bro. Sander
son (X), Bro. Chapman (0).
On motion, the meeting adjourned to Thursday,
May 12, 10 A. M.

THURSDAY, MAY 12, 1904

Bro. Johnston, Temporary President, called the Convention to order at 10
A. M. Minutes read and approved.
Bro. Bass, for the Committee on Credentials, reported that delegates from
the Beta and Kappa Chapters had not presented credentials. Credentials of
other delegates were furnished as follows :

Executive CouNCiiiHerbert Lawrence Bridgman {F '66).
Theta^ Arnold Goodwin Chapman, '06 ; George Chapman Newbury, '06.
Delta 

Francis Lewis Gould, '05.
Sigma 

Stephen Waterman Mason, '04.
GammaPaul Davie Storke, '04.
Zeta Hay ward Percival Rolfe, '04.

Lambda Kenneth Bulkley, '06.
Psi 

Howard Carter Dickinson, '05.
Xi 

Charles Akin Stone, '04.
Upsilon 
Howard Heermans Field, '04.
Iota Leland Alexander Vaughn, '04; Arthur James Larmon, '06.

Phi Morris Henry Stimson, '04; James Turner, '02 and '04.
Pi

Lang, '06 ; Harold Godfrey Cook, '07.

'04 ; Herbert Vanderhoof, '04 ; William Thomas Harsha, '06.
Epsilon Leo Delvin Bishop, '05 ; Edward Alexander Palmer, '07 ; Albert
Lee Clark, '07.
Graduate Delegate John Jameson Mapel, Phi, '72.

The report was accepted.

Bro. Baker reported for the Committee on Permanent Organization the
following nominations :
President
Herbert L. Bridgman {T '66).

Vice-Presidents

The report was accepted and Bro. Bridgman took the chair. The Conven
tion Rules of 1892 were adopted.
The Annual Communication of the Executive Council was read. The
President then appointed the following Standing Committees :

To Nominate an Executive Council Bros. Chapman
{&), Chairman,
Baker {T), Bishop {E), Dickinson {W), Rolfe (Z).
On the Annual Communication Bros. Turner
{$), Chairman, Vaughn
{I), Gramlich (71), (Gould {A), Barnard (H").
On Unfinished Business Bros. Bufflngton {BB), Chairman, Bass (M),
Field (r). Lord {fl), Fox (P).
On New Business Bros. Stone (S), Chairman, Storke (P), Mason (2),
Bulkley {A), Sanderson (X).

J

5

The President referred the Communication of the Executive Council to the
Committee on Annual Communication, and the Treasurer's Report and the
Petition of Chi Delta Psi Fraternity to the Committee on New Business.
Bro. Turner {$) presented two resolutions relating to Bro. Edward Martin
dale (0 '36) and Bro. Henry Clark Johnson (X '73), and requested their imme
diate consideration. The resolutions were unanimously adopted (Special
Resolutions Nos. 1 and 3). Bro. Bridgman spoke highly of our deceased Bro.
Johnson.
Bro. Turner ($) also offered a resolution for the appointment of a Commit
tee to invite the President of the University of Wisconsin to address the Con
vention. The resolution was adopted
(Special Resolution No. 3), and Bros.
Turner {$), Johnston (P) and
Mapel (P) were appointed such committee.
Bro. Fox (P) announced the death during the year of Bros. Edward Lawton
Van Ingen and John Van Ingen, of the Rho Chapter, Class of 1906.
Bro. Gould {A) announced the death of Bro. Jameson Northrop, Delta,
1901.
Bro. Bass (M) announced the death of Bro. Franklin Fiske Andrews,
Mu, 1898.
Bro. Bishop {E) stated that the Epsilon Chapter would like to hear of any
brothers on the Pacific coast, in order to keep the roster up to date.
Adjourned to Friday, May 13, 1904, 10 A. M.

FRIDAY, MAY 13, 1904

Meeting called to order by Bro. Bridgman.
Minutes read and approved.
The chairman of the Committee to nominate an Executive Council stated
that he was ready to report. At the request of the President Bro. Mapel (#),
Vice-President, took the chair. Bro Chapman (0) submitted the following
report, signed by the members of the Committee :
' '
The Committee to nominate an Executive Council would respectfully
offer the following resolutions for adoption by the Convention assembled :
1. Resolved, that a vote of thanks be extended to the retiring Executive
Council for their eminent services rendered to the Fraternity during the
past year.
2. Resolved, that the retiring Executive Council, composed of Brothers
H. L. Bridgman, Gamma '66,
Geo. S. Coleman, Xi '76,
G-eo. H. Fox, Upsilon '67,
Geo. W. Giddings, Lambda '93,
John V. Irwin, Delta '94,

he re-elected for the ensuing year."

6

On motion of Bro. Gould (A) the report of the Committee was adopted.
Brother Bridgman resumed the chair.
Bro. Turner ($) reported for the Committee on Annual Communication
various general and special resolutions, which were duly adopted {General
. Resolutions, Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4 ; Special Resolutions, Nos. 4, 5, 6, 7.)
The following General Resolution was also presented by the Committee ;

"Resolved, that each Chapter elect at the regular election of officers
at the fall term a member of a committee to be known as an Advisory
Committee, to act with the Executive Council ; such member to reside in
or near New Y^ork. In case of failure to elect such member, the Executive
Council shall be empowered to appoint a representative, and shall also be
empowered to fill any vacancy occurring during the year. As soon aa
possible after the election of the member to the Committee the Chapter
shall notify the Executive Council of such election."

After a general discussion of the resolution by Bros. Fox (P), Turner ($),
Lord {fh). Underwood (#), Gould {A), Bass (M), Willet M. Spooner (P), and
explanations by Bro. Bridgman, and an amendment by inserting the word
"preferably" after the word "reside,"' the resolution was lost on roU-cail of.
Chapters by a vote of eighteen to two.
Bro. Bufflngton {BB) reported for the Committee on Unfinished Business
resolutions concerning the Eleventh General Catalogue, and New Edition of
the Song Book, which were duly adopted {General Resolutions Nos. 5, 6).
Bro. Stone (S) reported for the Committee on New Business a resolution
rejecting the petition of the Cm Delta Psi Fraternity for a charter of Psi
Upsilon.
Bro. Fox (P) requested that the petition and application be read.
Bro. Spooner (P) asked whether it was desired to exclude entirely a Chap
ter from Canada.
Bro. Underwood {$) inquired what the policy of the Fraternity was in
regard to establishing Chapters outside the confines of the United States.
Bro. Dickinson {W) offered the following resolution :
"
Resolved, that it is not the policy of this fraternity to grant charters
outside of the confines of the United States."

Which on roll-call was carried unanimously {General Resolution No. 7).
Bro. Mapel (^) asked that an investigation be made of the Chi Delta Psi
Fraternity.
Upon roll-call, the resolution presented by Bro. Stone (3) for the Com
mittee on New Business, rejecting the petition of Chi Delta Psi, was
unanimously adopted {General Resolution No. 8).
A further resolution was submitted from the Committee on New Business,
authorizing the publication of matters relating to the Chapters and Fraternity

7

to be edited by the Executive Council. On motion of Bro. Storke (P) a

second paragraph was added to the resolution, and the resolution, as amended,
was adopted {General Resolution No. 9).
Bro. Lord {D,) recommends that the publication be sent to alumni.
Bro. Storke (P) asks that Chapter letters be still continued.
.
A resolution was adopted authorizing the levy of a tax upon the Chapters
for the general purposes of the Fraternity {General Resolution No. 10).
Bro. Turner {$) reported for the Special Committee that the President of
the University of Wisconsin was out of town and unable to address the
Convention.
The President announced that Bro. Albert P. Jacobs, of the Phi, would
be unable to respond to a toast at the banquet. Bro. Turner ($) was
appointed in his place.
Bro. Gramlich (i7) offered a resolution, which was adopted, providing for
notice to the Chapters, in advance of the Convention, of petitions from out
side colleges {General Resolution No. 11).
Bro. Vaughn (I) moved that a telegram be sent to Bro. Coleman, regretting
his absence. Carried.
Bro. Lord{D,) moved that an appropriate message be sent to Bro. Taft,
regretting his absence and illness. Carried.
Bro. Pox {P) announced the death (to-day) of Bro. Alva Stewart Goodyear,
Rho '97.
On motion of Bro. Turner ($), Bro. Henry (2) was chosen to respond to
the toast of the Undergraduates at the banquet.
Bro. Fox (P) offered a resolution as to the wearing of Psi Upsilon badges
by others than members of the Fraternity. Adopted {General Resolution
No. 12).
After singing "Dear Old Shrine," the Convention adjourned sine die.
JOHN W. MAPEL,-Rho '06,
Recorder.
RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED
GENBRA.L RESOLUTIONS

General Resolution No. 1. Resolved, That the report of the Treasurer of

the Executive Council be and is hereby approved.
General, Resolution No. 3. Resolved, That hereafter all signatures to the

Constitution be written in indelible ink.
General Resolution No. d. Resolved. That each Chapter send to the Ex

ecutive Council as soon as possible after these resolutions are received a list
of the printed Convention Records on hand, that the Council may aid in com
pleting the list by sending the missing copies.
General Resolution No. 4:. Resolved, That the designation of the time and
the
place of the meeting of the Convention in seventy-second year of the

8

Fraternity be referred by the Convention to the Executive Council, with the
request that the Chapters be definitely informed on or before January, 1905,
of the Chapter and date.
General Resolution No. 5. Resolved, That the Executive Council be and
hereby is authorized to reserve to itself twenty-five copies of the Eleventh
General Catalogue, and to forward remaining copies to each Chapter in pro
portion to the number of active men in each Chapter as shown by the Chapter
reports of February, 1904 ; the Executive Council to levy a special assess
_

ment upon each Chapter at the rate of one dollar each for all copies of cata

logues delivered.
General Resolution No. 6. Resolved, That the Convention re-adopt General

Resolution No. 6, passed by Convention of 1903, namely : That the Executive
Council be and hereby is authorized and requested to secure information from
the Chapters, during the coming year, as to such songs as the Chapters may
wish to have published in a new edition of the Fraternity Song Book, to
obtain estimates of the cost of a new edition, and to report to the next Con
vention such detailed facts as may enable the Convention to act properly in
the premises.

General Resolution No. 7. 

Resolved, That it is not the policy of this Fra
ternity to grant charters outside of the confines of the United States.
General Resolution No. 8. 

Resolved, That the petition of the Chi Delta Psi
Fraternity for admission into the Psi Upsilon Fraternity be rejected.
General Resolution No. 9. Resolved, That the Executive Council be

empowered to publish not less than two copies per year of a Psi Upsilon
publication devoted to Chapter news and Fraternity matters in general. This
publication shall contain a letter from each of the Chapters enumerating their
respective honors and general condition, and shall be edited by the Executive
Council.
Resolved, That each Chapter shall elect at the first meeting of the Fall
term an associate editor whose duties shall be the charge of his Chapter con
tribution to the publication.
General Resolution No. 10.Resolved, That the Executive Council be
empowered to levy a tax upon the Chapters at the rate of one dollar and a
quarter for each active member on the rolls on February 1st, 1905, for the
general purposes of the Fraternity.
General Resolution No. 11.Resolved, That the Executive Council here
after inform Chapters of any new petitions received from outside
colleges
before their delegates leave for the Convention.
General Resolution No. 13. Resolved, That the

utmost conservatism be
shown in allowing Psi Upsilon badges to be worn
by any other than members
of the Fraternity.

9

SPECIAL RESOLUTIONS.

Special Resolution No. 1. 

Resolved, That the following telegram be sent to
Brother Martindale
Madison, Wisconsin, I
May 12, 1904. >
Gen. Edward Martindale,
San Diego, California :

Convention, in Seventy-first year of Psi Upsilon, again salutes its
Founder, with honor and gratitude. May he and our Fraternity live long
and prosper.

Special Resolution No. 2. Resolved, That the death of Henry Clark John

son (Chi '73), deprives the Fraternity of one whose services in the Executive
Council and in the compilation and publication of the Tenth General Cata
logue will long be fruitful and memorable ; that his loyalty and enthusiasm
for Psi Upsilon will be a bright example for those who are to follow, and that
his name and his work will ever be honored in our records and treasured in
our hearts.

Special Resolution No, 3. 

Resolved, That the President of the Convention
is hereby requested to appoint a committee to present to the President of the
University of Wisconsin the respectful salutations of the Convention, and to
invite him to address it at a time convenient to him.

Special Resolution No. 4.

Resolved, That the thanks of the Fraternity are
due to Brother F. H. Hitchcock, Gamma '91, of the Grafton Press, who had
charge of the printing and binding of the copies of the Constitution, for the
excellent taste and careful attention to details which have produced such
satisfactory results.
Special Resolution No. 5. Resolved, That the Sixty-fourth Convention of

the Psi Upsilon Fraternity assembled at Madison, Wisconsin, May 11th to
13th, 1904, sends greeting to the Iota Chapter of Chi Psi Fraternity, and
extends thanks for the smoker and entertainment given to the members of this
Convention and Fraternity on the afternoon of Wednesday, May 11th, 1904.
Special Resolution No. 6.

Resolved, That the Convention regrets the fail
ure of the Beta and the Kappa to be represented in its session and work ;
that it suggests to the Council the propriety of an inquiry into the facts, with
the view of a statement to the next Convention ; to the end that precedents
contravening the Constitution be not established.
Special Resolution No. 7. Resolved, That the Convention return its sincere
thanks to the Rho Chapter of Psi Upsilon and to Brother Edward T. Owen,
Beta '72, for their generous hospitality, and that a proper letter of acknowl
edgment be transmitted by the Recorder of the Convention to Professor
Owen.

10

(APPBNDIX A)

THE COMMUNICATION OF THE EXECUTIVE COUNCIL TO
THE CONVENTION OF 1904

I. Membership. The active membership of the Fraternity on February
1, 1904, was 578, an increase of 15 since 1903.
II. In Memoriam. The following list of brethren who have passed
away since the last Convention is long and notable : J. Stanley Grimes, '40,
Curtis Coe Bean, '51, Edward Anthon, '54, Oscar Henry Curtis, '58, and
Charles James Fox, '61, of the Theta ; George Danielson Baker, '60, of the
Delta ; Albert Mathews, '43, David Hawley, '46, Samuel Clarke Perkins, '48,
Asa French and William De Forest Manice, '51, William Baldwin Ross, '53,
Lyman Dennison Brewster and Alfred Perkins Rockwell, '55, Burton Norvell Harrison, '59, William CollinsWhitney, '63, George Francis Lincoln,
'70, Ernest Rufus Adee, '85, and Edward Livingston Trudeau, Jr., '96, of
the Beta ; John Howard Sweetser, '57, and William Wellington Tyler, '64, of
the Gamma; Abiel Leonard, '70, of the Zeta; Frederic Renfe Coudert, '50,
Joseph Bayley Halsey, '68, Herbert Parsons, '79, Thomas Devlin O'Connor,
'81, and Guy Wetmore Carryl, '95, of the Lambda ; Egbert Coffin Smyth, '48,
and Edward Augustus Rand, '57, of the Kappa ; William Garrison White,
'85, of the Psi ; Jedediah Durkee Beeman, '64, of the Xi ; Joseph Lewis
Stackpole, '57, of the Alpha ; Walter Scott Bigelow, '89, of the Upsilon ;
Allen Briggs Seaman, '85, of the Omega; Alfred Ames Hewlett, '81, of the
Pi ; and Henry Clark Johnson, '73, of the Chi.

III. Copies of the Constitution. Pursuant to General Resolution No.
7 of the Convention of 1902, as modified by General Resolution No. 7 of the
Convention of 1903, sixty copies of the Constitution have been printed, and
two copies have been distributed to each of the chapters one
handsomely
bound in leather and provided with pages for signatures of initiates from the
class of 1904 to the class of 2004. the other bound in cloth and intended for
ordinary use. The Council would renew the suggestion that all be
signatures
written with indelible ink. The thanks of the
Fraternity are due to Brother
Frederick H. Hitchcock, Gamma '91, of the Grafton Press, who had charge
of the printing and binding, for the excellent taste and careful attention to
details which have produced such satisfactory results. The undistributed
copies of the Constitution are kept for possible future use. It is the hope of
the Council that the expense incurred for the copies distributed to the Chap
ters will be met by contributions from Alumni.

11

IV. Song Book. The Council would recommend that General Resolution
No. 6 of the Convention of 1903 be re-adopted. If the material for a new edi
tion is in hand by the end of the present year, appropriate action may be
taken at the next Convention, when the treasury will be in better condition
to stand the strain of publication.

V. Eleventh General Catalogue. There have been very few calls for
the new catalogue during the past year. As the value of the book is naturally
decreasing, it is timely to consider whether it would not be best to distribute
to the Chapters, pro rata, all the unsold copies (after reserving a certain num
ber for the archives), at a price to be fixed by the Convention. The proceeds of
the books would be covered into the treasury and become available for general
Fraternltj'' uses.
In this connection it may be noted that if the annual leaflet of new mem
bers authorized by General Resolution No. 4 of 1903 shall be published, the
owners of copies of the latest catalogue will be able to keep the list of mem
bers up to date. The leaflet was not published last year because it was
deemed prudent to incur no extra expenses pending the printing of the Con
stitution. But the first leafiet published should, of course, contain the names
added to the rolls since February 1, 1902.

VI. Seventieth Anniversary. Pursuant to General Resolution No. 9
of 1903, the seventieth anniversary of the founding of the Fraternity was duly
celebrated by a reception and banquet at the Waldorf-Astoria, New York, on
Tuesday evening, November 34, 1903.
The large and representative attendance, the songs and speeches, the letters
from the Chapters, and from brethren unable to be present, including Brother
Martindale, combined to make the occasion memorable. Printed souvenirs
of the banquet have been distributed to the Chapters, and copies are still
available for those who may wish them.

VII.Printed Records op Contention. In our last annual communi
cation (paragraph VIII) attention was called to the fact that there remain
in the archives duplicate copies of the Convention records from 1876 to 1903
inclusive. It is very desirable that flies of these records be carefully pre
served by the Chapters. It is also believed that it would be well if the Chap
ters would consider at some regular meeting in the fall term of each year the

printedrecords of the Convention of that year, so that any action called for
undertaken.
by the resolutions adopted might be promptly

IX. Application tor Chapter. A fourth petition has been presented
for a Charter of the Fraternity at the University of Toronto, Canada. The
petitioners have, since the last Convention, adopted an associate name Ohi

Delta Psi. The petition and accompanying letter are herewith submitted.

X. Advisory Committee. The Council would submit to the Conven
tion for consideration the propriety and expediency of establishing a commit
tee consisting of graduate member of each of the Chapters, residing in
one

or near New York, to act as an
advisory board with the Executive Council ;
the committee to be elected annually by the Chapters, or, in default of such

election, to be appointed by the Council. It has been suggested that such a
committee, being in close touch with the undergraduates, might be able to
recommend from time to time appropriate action tending to advance the
interests of the Fraternity.

XI. Treasurer's Report. The report of the Treasurer is presented
herewith.

Respectfully submitted.

(APPENDIX E)

Letter Accompanying Petition

97 St. Joseph St., Toronto,
May 3rd, 1904.
The Executive Council of the
PsiUpsilon Fraternity.
Sirs :

We are mailing to you herewith our fourth petition to the Psi
Upsilon Fraternity.
Since our last application we have taken the name of Chi Delta Psi and
have adopted a fraternity pin, these steps being taken mainly for the benefit
of our undergraduate members, -who felt the inconvenience of belonging to a

fraternity without an official name. That the organization is the same which
has petitioned you formerly will be readily seen from the signatures attached
to our several petitions.
We continue to occupy the fraternity house with which we have been
identified for the last three years, and during the past year have initiated six
new members. Our fraternity now has a total membership of thirty-six,
made up as follows :
undergraduate members, fifteen ; active graduate
members, ten; inactive graduate members, eleven. In the number of active
graduate members we include only those who are resident in Toronto and
continue to take an active part in fraternity meetings and general work ;

a large proportion of the number are either entered as students at the Law
School or are pursuing post-graduate work. The number of inactive mem
bers is made up of those who by reason of their absence from the city, or
occupation in business are prevented from entering into our fraternity life.
They continue bound however by their fraternal ties.
In Athletics, during the past year, we have been successful, though not
unusually so for us. Members of our fraternity have held places on the
Senior Football, Hockey, Lacrosse and Baseball teams, and one of our mem
bers, Mr. Sherry, had the honor of being elected to a place on the Athletic
Directorate of the University, which is the controlling body over all college

we are proud of the fact that the last holder of the scholarship, Mr. W. C.

Our men have also taken their share in the general life of the University,
and we are represented, as we always have been, on the Executive of the
'Varsity Literary Society which is the controlling body in our University
affairs. Mr. McKay, another of our members, has been selected as sporting
editor of the college newspaper for the coming year.
We believe that the University of Toronto is now sufficiently well known
to render proofs of its standing unnecessary. We believe also that the facts
which we have already stated show that our fraternity holds a high place in the
University. On both of these matters we invite and desire the closest scrutiny.
We may say that in the last year we have received overtures from two general
fraternities both of which were promptly rejected by us. We do not state
this in any boastful spirit nor with the expectation that it will in any way
influence your convention, but merely to show that our position is recognized
within the University and even beyond it. We believe further that our rejec
tion of these advances is evidence of the strong spirit of loyalty and independ
ence, which from the first has animated our fraternity. We are convinced of
the permanency of our organization, and it is our intention either to become
a constituent part of the very best and strongest general
fraternity, or to
remain in a state of honorable independence.
For the first time in three years we shall not be represented by delegates at
your convention, having decided to let our present petition and this letter
speak for themselves. We rest assured that although not personally pre
sented, they will be received with the same courtesy and consideration which
we have always enjoyed at the hands of the Psi
Upsilon Fraternity.
We remain,
